codeReview.summary: The snapshot-based doctor path correctly avoids filesystem writes for normal cases, but it still has two correctness gaps: it can under-report unhealthy databases when config is unavailable, and it can crash on an existing DB that lacks the metadata table because read-only inspection no longer bootstraps schema.

issues.description: When `args.fingerprint` is null, `getDoctorReport()` skips `inspectIndexState()` and falls back to only checking `failedSourceManifests`. That means an existing DB with missing search tables or a stale fingerprint can be reported as `healthStatus: 'ok'` if the config cannot be loaded, violating the requirement that `db doctor` report an accurate health/rebuild status for any existing DB.

`getDbStats()` still unconditionally calls `getStoredFingerprint(db)`, which queries `index_metadata` without a guard. Because `db doctor` now opens a raw read-only snapshot instead of bootstrapping schema, an existing DB file that lacks `index_metadata` (for example, a partially initialized or manually created file) will now throw instead of returning a doctor report.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The worker deviated from the skill's 'tests first' procedure while iterating on SQLite/WAL snapshot behavior. The handoff says this was intentional because the read-only doctor fix needed implementation context before stable regression tests could be written.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: handoff.skillFeedback.followedProcedure=false; deviations explain the implementation-first step before tests.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The doctor implementation now depends on a temp snapshot copy of the DB plus `-wal/-shm` sidecars to stay read-only. This pattern is not recorded in `.factory/library/`, so future DB-read-only work may need to rediscover it.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/commands/shared.ts:172-194 copies the DB and sidecars into a temp dir before opening it readonly.

summary: Review completed for `db-doctor-rebuild-health-and-fingerprint-guards`; the feature is close, but the doctor path still has correctness gaps that can misreport or crash on existing DBs.
